book_title: Prologue: The Business, The Price & Our Independent Verdict
question: What does Mondelēz International do, why is it inflecting now, and why do we wait for $63.35–$64.50 support?

epigraph.quote: Great consumer franchises rarely go on sale during clear skies; the edge belongs to the analyst who separates temporary commodity storms from permanent brand erosion—and waits for asymmetric entry.
epigraph.author: Mondelez Underwriting Synthesis

web_blocks.html: What Mondelēz Does: Mondelēz International (NASDAQ: MDLZ) is a global pure-play snacking leader. It generated $38.54 billion in FY2025 revenue across 150+ countries [4][10]. Biscuits & Baked Snacks account for 47.7% of sales (Oreo, Ritz, LU, Clif Bar), while Chocolate adds 32.9% (Cadbury, Milka, Toblerone) and Gum & Candy adds 10.5% [4][20]. Roughly 40% of revenue comes from emerging markets, including 5 million+ outlets in India and 1 million+ stores in Brazil [12][28].

Independent Dual Verdict: Pass 1 awarded MDLZ a price-blind COMPOUNDER_PASS (PASS_WITH_WATCH KPI health). Pass 2 assigns a New-Capital Verdict of WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT (CORE_ALPHA, TIER_2) at CMP $66.28 (Nov 20, 2026). Grounding our Base Target at $71.50 (21.0x $3.40 normalized FY27E EPS, aligned with $70.42 consensus) leaves only 1.08:1 CMP asymmetry against our $61.43 stop. Waiting for a pullback to $63.35–$64.50 restores asymmetry to 2.28:1. Our positions ledger confirms MDLZ is NOT_HELD (0 shares).

web_blocks.html: Bull vs. Bear in One Minute: Bulls point to Q3 2026's inflection: volume/mix rose +1.8 percentage points, adjusted gross margin expanded +380 bps YoY to 34.2%, and ~70% of revenue held or gained share [37][38]. Bears note Q3 relied on -3.7 pp EU price cuts, North America vol/mix was flat, 9M26 payouts ($2.8B) exceeded FCF ($1.66B) by $1.14B, and $1.2B ERP costs cap normalized OM near 16.5% [12][27][29]. Our view: own MDLZ on a pullback to $63.35–$64.50, not at $66.28.

book_paragraphs: Every time you walk past a supermarket end-cap stacked with Oreo cookies, Ritz crackers, or Cadbury Dairy Milk bars, you are looking at one of the most resilient distribution machines in global consumer packaged goods. Mondelēz International generates $38.54 billion in annual revenue across more than 150 countries, with roughly 40% of its sales rooted in emerging markets—including over 5 million retail outlets in India and 1 million stores in Brazil—where modern snacking penetration still has decades of runway.

For the past two years, however, Mondelēz was trapped in an extraordinary raw-material storm. Historic West African cocoa shortages sent bean prices vertical, compressing GAAP gross margins by over 1,000 basis points in FY2025 and forcing management to choose between protecting short-term profits and defending shelf space. The stock de-rated as low as 17.36 times earnings while investors debated whether chocolate and biscuit demand had been permanently impaired by price elasticity and GLP-1 adoption.

That debate turned a corner in Q3 2026. Volume and mix—the purest pulse of consumer demand—inflected to +1.8 percentage points, its strongest showing in nearly three years, while adjusted gross margin jumped 380 basis points year-over-year to 34.2% and roughly 70% of revenue held or gained market share. At $66.28 per share as of November 20, 2026, Mondelēz trades at 20.89 times trailing earnings and 19.76 times forward earnings, paying a 3.05% dividend.

Yet great underwriting requires separating a great business from an asymmetric entry price. When we ground our Base Case in Mondelēz's actual 16.2% historical operating margin ceiling and $1.2 billion ERP investment program through 2028, realistic normalized earnings power is $3.40 per share, supporting a $71.50 Base Target at 21.0x (in line with Wall Street's $70.42 consensus). At $66.28, $71.50 offers only 1.08-to-1 reward-to-risk against our $61.43 stop—below our 1.50-to-1 hurdle—while 6 stock-level distribution days and a US Downtrend regime sit overhead. Because our positions ledger shows zero shares held (NOT_HELD), we assign WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT: keep 100% in Treasury cash today and deploy on a pullback into $63.35–$64.50, where reward-to-risk jumps to 2.28-to-1.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: How to Read This 10-Chapter Monograph
book_callouts.quote: Chapters 1 through 6 were written completely blind to the stock price—and Chapters 7 through 9 refused to stretch valuation assumptions to justify chasing CMP.
book_callouts.text: As you read through this dossier, notice how the two-pass architecture works: Chapters 1–6 prove Mondelēz is a COMPOUNDER_PASS business; Chapters 7–9 show why $63.35–$64.50—not $66.28—is the disciplined price to pay.
